title: CDIF DCAT-Syntax Core and Discovery Profiles: Development Plan
content:
CDIF DCAT-Syntax Core and Discovery Profiles: Development Plan: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22942627 

This document is the first in an irregular series of updates on development plans for the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF). It briefly outlines the status and intended process for development of CDIF Core and Discovery profiles based on the W3C DCAT specification, as opposed to Schema.org. While Schema.org was initially chosen as the basis for core CDIF metadata, given its widespread adoption and support in various search engines and other widely used Web-based applications, the need for a similar foundation implemented using DCAT has become apparent, as its adoption is now becoming much broader.

The intention is that a point-for-point correspondence between the two sets of profiles — for DCAT on the one hand and for Schema.org on the other — can be established, and that free converters provided to enable users to produce and consume either flavour as needed. While a single agreed standard is always ideal, it is not in this case a reality, so this approach is seen as necessary.

title: LAST CHANCE TO REGISTER! An AI-ready, data engineering playbook for FAIR Integration in EOSC and beyond: CDIF4EOSC Workshop, London, Friday 9 October
content:
Registration will close at 09:00 UTC Friday 25 September.

Register here to attend in person: https://forms.gle/CSmL6kcxJerWPPuV7

In person registration is open for this informative and interactive workshop about the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF) and the CDIF4EOSC project. The workshop is being held as an RDA 27th Plenary Meeting Co-located Event.

Date: Friday, 9th October 2026
Time: 09:30-16:00 BST
Location: The Long Room, Kia Oval Cricket Ground
Format: In person only

Details: The distinct approach of the CDIF4EOSC project is to build on the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF). The project will extend the CDIF recommendations, adding profiles and guidelines, and use case based examples, to form a comprehensive and actionable playbook for FAIR Integration in the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) and beyond.

title: Career Opportunities at CODATA! Deadline approaching, 28 September
content:
Excellent opportunities for experienced professionals seeking a full-time, fixed-term role and eager to work in an innovative international team of experts to advance science and the use of data to address today’s global, multifaceted societal challenges.

CODATA is recruiting for two roles:

  • Project officer, Data Policy, Legal and Organisational Interoperability
  • Technical Expert, Data, Metadata and Trustworthy AI

    • Please see the further details for each role on the CODATA website.

    Applicants are requested to address the job description, qualifications, knowledge and skills requirements in a cover letter (maximum two pages), which should include summaries and links to relevant work; and a curriculum vitae (maximum four pages) with the name and contact details of three referees; and a sample document summarising a recent project or contributions to an open source initiative). Deadline for applications, 28 September 2026.

    Questions can be directed to apply@codata.org.

    Applications should ONLY be submitted via email to apply@codata.org.  Incomplete applications will not be considered.
